title: Entities and conventions
summary: How EF Core decides table names, keys, column types and nullability without being told.

steps.title: Convention over configuration
body: You never told EF Core that `Books` is a table, that `Id` is the primary key, or that `Title` is text. It worked that out from your classes. These rules are **conventions**:
- A `DbSet<Book>` property named `Books` maps to a table named `Books`.
- A property named `Id` (or `BookId`) becomes the **primary key**. An `int` key is generated by the database.
- Every public property with a getter and a setter becomes a **column**, named like the property.
- C# types pick column types: `int` becomes `INTEGER`, `string` becomes `TEXT`, and `bool` becomes `INTEGER` (0 or 1) in SQLite.
- **Nullability follows C#**: a `string` is a required column (`NOT NULL`), a `string?` is optional (`NULL`). The same goes for `int` against `int?`.
A class EF Core maps to a table is an **entity type**, and each object of it is an **entity**.

steps.prompt: Match each piece of C# to what EF Core makes of it by convention.
pairs: Primary key, generated by the database
steps.explain: Names come from your code, and `?` decides whether the column allows `NULL`.

steps.title: See the schema
body: `db.Database.GenerateCreateScript()` returns the SQL that `EnsureCreated` would run. It is the quickest way to check what EF Core made of your classes.
"Id" INTEGER NOT NULL CONSTRAINT "PK_Books" PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
`PK_Books` is the name of the primary-key constraint. `AUTOINCREMENT` is how SQLite generates the ids.

steps.prompt: What does this print? (`Contains` checks the generated script for a piece of text.)
steps.explain: `Subtitle` is a `string?`, so its column allows `NULL`. `Pages` is a plain `int`, so it is `INTEGER NOT NULL`. `Title` is a non-nullable `string`: `TEXT NOT NULL`.

steps.prompt: A class named `Book` has a property `public int BookId { get; set; }` and no `Id`. What does EF Core do?
options: Treats `BookId` as a foreign key to another table
steps.explain: `Id` and `<ClassName>Id` are both key conventions. With neither, EF Core throws when it builds the model: every entity needs a key (or must be marked keyless).
`Name` is a non-nullable `string`, so the column is `NOT NULL`. `null!` silences the compiler, but the database still refuses the row, and EF Core reports that as a `DbUpdateException`.

steps.title: Properties that are not columns
body: Only properties with a getter **and** a setter are mapped. A computed, read-only property is ignored, which is what you want for derived values:
public bool IsClassic => Year < 1950;    // not a column: no setter
If you need a settable property that should *not* be stored, mark it `[NotMapped]`.
Fields, methods and private properties are not mapped either. An entity is an ordinary class: you can give it behaviour.

steps.title: Map a recipe
prompt: Write a `Recipe` entity and a `KitchenDb` context (`Data Source=kitchen.db`, a `DbSet<Recipe>` named `Recipes`) so that the generated table is:
"Id" INTEGER NOT NULL CONSTRAINT "PK_Recipes" PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
Also give `Recipe` a read-only property `bool IsQuick` that is true when `PrepMinutes` is under 15. It must **not** become a column.
template: Dojo.Check("Name is TEXT NOT NULL", dojoSql.Contains("\"Name\" TEXT NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Notes is TEXT NULL", dojoSql.Contains("\"Notes\" TEXT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Servings is INTEGER NOT NULL", dojoSql.Contains("\"Servings\" INTEGER NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("PrepMinutes is INTEGER NULL", dojoSql.Contains("\"PrepMinutes\" INTEGER NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("IsQuick is not a column", !dojoSql.Contains("IsQuick"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Id is the primary key", dojoSql.Contains("\"PK_Recipes\" PRIMARY KEY"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Eq("IsQuick for 10 minutes", true, new Recipe { PrepMinutes = 10 }.IsQuick);
Dojo.Eq("IsQuick for 30 minutes", false, new Recipe { PrepMinutes = 30 }.IsQuick);
Dojo.Eq("IsQuick with no time given", false, new Recipe().IsQuick);
hints: `PrepMinutes < 15` on an `int?` is false when it is null, which is what you want.
